COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
06.04.2023 WPMB No. 17 of 2023
Hon’ble Vipin Sanghi, C.J.
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Mr. Himanshu Pal, learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
Issue notice. 
Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned Standing Counsel for 
the Union of India, appears and accepts notice on 
behalf of all the respondents. 
The petitioner has preferred the present Writ 
Petition to seek the following reliefs :-
“i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus commanding/ directing the respondent nos. 1, 
2 & 3 to adhere to the contract dated 13.02.2023 and 
proceed further as per the contract.
ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus commanding/ directing the respondent nos. 1, 
2 & 3 to accept the bank guarantee in lieu of letter dated 
06.03.20239 (A11).
iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
Certiorari, quashing the impugned order dated 22.03.2023 
(A14), whereby the contract awarded in the favour of 
petitioner was cancelled.
iv) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of 
mandamus commanding/ directing the CBI/CVC to conduct 
an enquiry regarding malpractices in grant of government 
contracts/tenders to favorable bidders/ contractors.”
The petitioner participated in the tender invited 
by the respondent-AIIMS, Rishikesh for providing 
dietary services at AIIMS, Rishikesh. The petitioner 
participated in the said tender, and was adjudged as L2 
bidder. Since the L1 bidder did not accept the contract, 
it was awarded to the petitioner on 13.02.2023. The 
contract was executed with the petitioner on  13.02.2023. On 06.03.2023 the respondents asked 
the petitioner to furnish a bank guarantee within 15 
days, of the amount of Rs. 21.68 lacs. The petitioner 
states that the petitioner procured the bank guarantee 
from its bank, and offered the same to the 
respondents. However, the same was not accepted. 
The petitioner also sent representations. Eventually, 
the respondents have taken the stand that, since the 
petitioner had not submitted the bank guarantee, the 
contract had been cancelled. The bank guarantee had 
been procured by the petitioner before the expiry of 15 
days on 18.03.2023, whereas the 15 days’ period 
granted to the petitioner were to expire on 21.03.2023.
Therefore, prima facie, it does not make any 
sense, as to why the petitioner would procure the bank 
guarantee, and not furnish the same. The petitioner 
had also sent a representation to the respondents on 
22.03.2023, stating that he had prepared the bank 
guarantee, and offered the same in time. 
Prima facie, it appears to us that the action of the 
respondents is arbitrary. The respondents are directed 
to file their counter affidavit(s) within four weeks. 
The respondents shall maintain status quo in the 
meantime. 
List on 17.05.2023.
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Vipin Sanghi, C.J.)
 06.04.2023 06.04.2023
Rahul

Mr. Himanshu Pal, Advocate for the

(2) Ms. Neeti Rana, Standing Counsel for 
respondent nos. 2, 3 and 4.
(3) The stand taken by the petitioner is 
that a binding contract was entered into 
between him and AIIMS, Rishikesh.
Pleadings to this effect are made in 
paragraph 12 of the writ petition. 
Annexure-10 to the writ petition is a 
document, which according to the 
petitioner, is the contract.
(4) Learned counsel for petitioner has 
drawn our attention to the bottom-line of 
said contract, where, it is mentioned that 
this is system generated file.
(5) Ms. Neeti Rana, Advocate is not able 
to give any satisfactory reply, as to 
whether the document enclosed as 
Annexure-10, is a binding contract or not. 
She is also not able to answer as to 
whether signatures of both the parties 
would be required on the contract or not.  Although, a short counter affidavit is filed 
on behalf of the AIIMS, Rishikesh, 
however, no reply to the pleadings made 
in paragraph 12 to the writ petition is 
given.
(6) In such view of the matter, we direct 
Director, AIIMS, Rishikesh to file 
supplementary counter affidavit positively 
within a period of ten days, failing which, 
he shall appear in person before this Court 
on the next date of listing.
(7) List this matter on 24.08.2023.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) 
09.08.2023

--Petitioner
 Versus
Union Of India Through Ministry Of Helath 
And Family Welfare New Delhi
--Respondent
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Himanshu Pal, learned counsel for the 
petitioner. 
2. Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned Standing Counsel for 
AIIMS, Rishikesh. 
3. Petitioner responded to a Notice Inviting Tender 
issued by AIIMS, Rishikesh for the work of dietary 
services. His bid was found to be the second lowest, 
but since the one with lowest bid was declared 
technically disqualified, therefore, petitioner’s bid 
became the lowest. 
4. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that, after 
generation of contract through Government e￾Marketplace (GeM), petitioner went to the competent 
authority in AIIMS, Rishikesh to submit bank 
guarantee, however, bank guarantee was not accepted 
from him, and five days thereafter, petitioner received 
an email dated 22.03.2023, whereby petitioner was 
informed that the buyer has cancelled its contract 
GEMC-511687731462992 because EPBG or transaction 
charges have not been paid by him within the 
stipulated time. Thus, feeling aggrieved, petitioner 
filed this Writ Petition challenging the cancellation order 
dated 22.03.2023. 5. A counter affidavit is filed by Gaurav Badola, 
Administrative Officer, AIIMS, Rishikesh. However, in 
paragraph no. 4 of the counter affidavit, it is mentioned 
that the contract was cancelled due to substantial 
change in scope of work and inadvertent omission of 
some clauses. Paragraph no. 4 of the said counter 
affidavit is extracted below :
“4. That GeM bid was proposed for cancellation by 
Buyer, AIIMS Rishikesh due to required substantial change 
in scope of work and inadvertent omission of some clauses 
(e.g; Guidelines for Modern Kitchen and Dietary Services, 
2022, issued by Department of Health and Family Welfare, 
Government of India) through GeM portal on 13.02.2023 
and the same was accepted by seller i.e; petitioner on
14.02.2023. Therefore it was a mutual decision to scrap 
this tender. Hence, respondents were not legally bound to 
accept the PBG against the tender which stood cancelled. 
Copy of the relevant GeM Document regarding acceptance 
of cancellation of tender by petitioner dated 14.02.2023 is 
enclosed as Annexure # SCA-1.”
6. Thus, the reason assigned for cancelling the 
contract, as indicated in the email dated 22.03.2023, 
does not match with the reason assigned in paragraph 
no. 4 of the counter affidavit. This indicates that there 
is something more to it than what meets the eye.
7. We, therefore, call upon the Director, AIIMS, 
Rishikesh to file his personal affidavit, explaining the 
matter. Such affidavit shall be filed on or before 
17.11.2026. 
8. List on 18.11.2026.
9. In case such affidavit is not filed within stipulated 
time, then the Director, AIIMS, Rishikesh shall appear 
in person, along with entire record of the case, before 
this Court on 19.11.2026.
 (Subhash Upadhyay, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.) 
 29.10.2026 29.10.2026
Rahul
